open_findings.summary: provider and tool URL validation checks the hostname string, not the address actually reached, so a name resolving to an internal address passes. Exploitation requires provider.manage or agent.manage.
file extraction is routed by extension and client-declared MIME type with no magic-byte sniffing. A correctness limitation, not an execution risk.
the extractor 48 MiB ingestion limit is unreachable through the JSON API: base64 inflates it to exactly the 64 MiB body cap, so body() rejects first and mid-upload.
a full workspace backup is not encrypted and contains the auth master key. The product data export does exclude credentials; a filesystem backup is an operator duty that the documentation must state.

open_findings.summary: The product has never been measured against MASTER PROJECT V4. 46 of its 121 files, including the acceptance matrix, implementation gates, traceability matrix and Owner review checklist, were never brought into the repository. Against that matrix two blockers are open (SEC-003 never tested; OPS-002 covers one platform family of five) and several required features are absent - Workflows, the approval queue, passkeys/OIDC/SAML/SCIM, two of the seven privacy states, compliance packs, the industry module framework, ML-BOM and any WCAG 2.2 AA evidence. Separately, /api/v1/bootstrap advertises Workflows as a feature that does not exist.

The deployed WebUI diverges from DESIGN/APPROVED_WEBUI_REFERENCE.png, which 01_PRODUCT/11 calls binding: no central composer, no quick actions, no active-tasks panel and no bottom approval strip on Home, and 21 flat nav entries against the spec rule of simple-before-technical progressive disclosure. The specification also requires visual regression and Owner review before the UI is final; neither has happened. A reorganised prototype (26 destinations in 5 categories, 9 selectable themes) is published for the Owner decision.

resolved_findings.summary: createDecipheriv(aes-256-gcm) called without {authTagLength:16}, then setAuthTag() on a stored attacker-influenceable value. Node accepts 4-16 byte GCM tags, so a truncated tag drops authentication from 128 to 32 bits. Contextual severity medium: requires prior write access to the workspace credential store. Defence-in-depth in the credential vault; cheap to fix; product is not installed or running.
resolved_findings.fix: pass {authTagLength:16} to createDecipheriv and validate the decoded tag length is exactly 16 before setAuthTag, at all 4 sites
resolved_findings.found_by: semgrep via noesar-debuglab, first HUNT AND FIX sweep
resolved_findings.fix_applied: authTagLength pinned to GCM_TAG_BYTES=16 on both createCipheriv and createDecipheriv, plus an explicit tag-length check before setAuthTag, at all 4 sites
resolved_findings.evidence: vulnerability reproduced first (a 4-byte tag decrypted successfully before the fix); 8 new regression tests in services/reference-control-plane/test/gcm-tag-length.test.mjs; full product suite 137/137 pass (was 129 delivered + 8 new); semgrep re-scan of services/ and ai-workspace/ reports 0 gcm-no-tag-length findings

resolved_findings.summary: All three delivered installers use --mount type=bind,...,rw, which Docker 29 rejects: invalid field rw must be a key=value pair. Every installer would fail on this host.
Inside a container /etc/localtime describes the image, not the host, so tier 3 of the timezone chain shadowed the installer TZ with Etc/UTC and the operator setting was silently ignored.

resolved_findings.summary: the temporary start of noesar-debuglab modified its own ephemeral container layer (25 files: bytecode caches, semgrep settings, a detect-secrets temp file). Host data unchanged, before and after both phases. The phase 3 claim was true of host data and over-broad at container level.

a TOTP code could be replayed within the +/-1 step window, defeating the second factor for up to 90 seconds. Fixed with per-user single-use step enforcement across setup, login and step-up, persisted across restarts. 8 regression tests; AUTH-19 now PASS.

reported as an SSE stream aborting with no error frame; the test written to prove it passed against unmodified code. The abort was caused by F4-004 killing the process. Recorded because it was reported before it was verified.

POST /api/v1/chat/stream was invoked without await, so a rejection became an unhandled rejection and terminated the process. One malformed request from any session with provider.use killed the service. Fixed by awaiting, validating before writing SSE headers, making json() safe when headers are sent, and adding process-level guards. 5 regression tests including one that asserts the child process survives.

ProviderGateway.probe() referenced an undeclared providerId, so a reachable provider reported 500 while an unreachable one reported a tidy 502. Only the failure path had ever executed. 3 regression tests.

streamWithFallback() referenced the same undeclared providerId, throwing a ReferenceError on the first delta of every stream: streaming chat had never worked, always returning exactly two SSE frames. After the fix the same request returns nine. 9 regression tests covering every public gateway method.
fetch transport failures were propagated as the single word "fetch failed", discarding error.cause and making a provider outage undiagnosable. Adding cause reporting is what made F4-009 findable.

two security-matrix rows described behaviour the code does not have: CORS cited a test file containing no CORS test, and user/project isolation claimed IMPLEMENTED while the reference data plane has no per-user ownership and no route creates a second user. Both rewritten to the real mechanism; per-project isolation verified live with a canary.

a pooled keep-alive socket already closed by the upstream surfaced as a user-visible stream error with no retry. First hypothesis (idle timing) was tested and refuted; the real signature appeared only after F4-007. Fixed with a single narrowly-scoped retry. SEC-27 and SEC-30 now PASS.
